Events.RelatedDescription: Opened issue "FSA diagnostics cache ignores analyzer filter changes on an unchanged project" (#86334) at dotnet/roslyn
Events.RelatedBody:
### Description

Closed-file full-solution analysis (FSA) diagnostics can remain stale when compiler or analyzer diagnostic scopes change without changing the project snapshot. Fresh diagnostic pulls continue to return results computed using the previous analyzer filter.

Observed with the Roslyn language server bundled by dotnet/vscode-csharp:
- Version: `5.14.0-1.26552.2`
- Source revision: `eb07b178c241fad780d6fc947512f00bbdbd1dc4`
- Environment: VS Code on macOS, standalone C# extension (without C# Dev Kit)

The same cache implementation was also present in upstream `main` when investigated.

### Reproduction

Use a closed C# file containing both compiler and analyzer diagnostics, for example the [vscode-csharp diagnostics fixture](https://github.com/dotnet/vscode-csharp/blob/main/test/lsptoolshost/integrationTests/testAssets/slnWithCsproj/src/app/diagnostics.cs).

Keep `dotnet.backgroundAnalysis.analyzerDiagnosticsScope` set to `fullSolution` throughout:

1. Set `dotnet.backgroundAnalysis.compilerDiagnosticsScope` to `fullSolution`. Pull workspace diagnostics to populate the cache.
2. Change compiler scope to `none`, without editing any files, and pull diagnostics again.
3. Add and save whitespace in an unrelated C# file in the same project, then pull diagnostics again.
4. Change compiler scope back to `fullSolution`, without another edit, and pull diagnostics again.
5. Add and save another whitespace edit in the unrelated file, then pull diagnostics again.

The diagnostic target remained closed, and the language-server PID remained unchanged throughout the controlled reproduction.

| Step | Expected | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| Both scopes full solution | 5 diagnostics, including compiler warning `CS0219` | 5 |
| Compiler scope changed to none | 4 diagnostics, without `CS0219` | Still 5, including `CS0219` |
| Unrelated whitespace edit saved | 4 | 4 |
| Compiler scope changed back to full solution | 5, including `CS0219` | Still 4, missing `CS0219` |
| Second unrelated whitespace edit saved | 5 | 5 |

The five initial diagnostic codes were `CA1822`, `CS0219`, `IDE0005`, `IDE0059`, and `IDE0130`.

### Configuration and diagnostic freshness

This was reproduced while removing unnecessary server restarts from vscode-csharp integration tests. To rule out client timing and cached diagnostic collections, the experiment:

- Awaited forwarding of the final configuration notification.
- Sent `workspace/waitForAsyncOperations` after that notification to wait for server processing/background work.
- Requested full workspace diagnostic reports by omitting previous result IDs.
- Inspected newly returned reports through the normal language-client diagnostic pipeline, rather than relying only on existing VS Code diagnostic collections.

The returned full reports themselves contained the stale diagnostic set. Restarting the server, or changing the project snapshot through the unrelated edit, made the scopes take effect.

### Suspected root cause

[`AbstractWorkspaceDocumentDiagnosticSource.FullSolutionAnalysisDiagnosticSource`](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/eb07b178c241fad780d6fc947512f00bbdbd1dc4/src/LanguageServer/Protocol/Handler/Diagnostics/DiagnosticSources/AbstractWorkspaceDocumentDiagnosticSource.cs#L35) caches diagnostics using:

```csharp
ConditionalWeakTable<Project, AsyncLazy<ILookup<DocumentId, DiagnosticData>>>
```

The cached `AsyncLazy` captures `analyzerFilter` when it calls `GetDiagnosticsForIdsAsync`. However, `analyzerFilter` is not part of the cache identity. A subsequent source for the same `Project` instance but a different filter therefore reuses diagnostics calculated under the previous filter.

[`WorkspaceDocumentsAndProjectDiagnosticSourceProvider`](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/eb07b178c241fad780d6fc947512f00bbdbd1dc4/src/LanguageServer/Protocol/Handler/Diagnostics/DiagnosticSourceProviders/WorkspaceDocumentsAndProjectDiagnosticSourceProvider.cs) derives the filter from the current compiler/analyzer FSA scopes, so configuration changes can alter the filter without replacing the project instance.

The project-level diagnostic source does not use this particular cache; this report concerns closed-document FSA diagnostics.

### Suggested fix and regression coverage

Include `AnalyzerFilter` in the cache identity while preserving weak references to project instances and sharing cached computations across documents for the same project/filter.

Add regression tests that populate the real FSA source cache, then independently change compiler and analyzer scopes on the same project snapshot, in both directions, without file edits or server restarts. The existing [FSA on/off tests](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/eb07b178c241fad780d6fc947512f00bbdbd1dc4/src/LanguageServer/ProtocolUnitTests/Diagnostics/PullDiagnosticTests.cs#L2296) toggle both scopes together; they do not exercise a changed analyzer filter while FSA remains enabled.

### Impact

Users can continue seeing diagnostics that should have been disabled, or fail to see newly enabled diagnostics, until the project snapshot changes. This also currently prevents removing per-case server restarts from the closed-file diagnostics integration tests in dotnet/vscode-csharp.

```

```

`dotnet store -h`

### Expected behavior

Assuming it is deprecated, the following would work. If it is not deprecated then fix MSLearn. 

Alternatively, you could both add this to the description and mark the command as obsolete so it does not show up. 

```
Description:
  ** 
  Warning! The dotnet store command and the runtime package store feature are deprecated and no longer supported. 
  ***
  Stores the specified assemblies for the .NET Platform. By default, these will be optimized for the target runtime and
  framework.

  dotnet store [<argument>...] [options]

  -o, --output <OUTPUT_DIR>                The output directory to store the given assemblies in.
  -w, --working-dir <WORKING_DIR>          The working directory used by the command to execute.
  --skip-optimization                      Skip the optimization phase. [default: False]

  -r, --runtime <RUNTIME_IDENTIFIER>       The target runtime to store packages for.
  -v, -verbosity <LEVEL>                   Set the MSBuild verbosity level. Allowed values are q[uiet], m[inimal],

  --ucr, --use-current-runtime             Use current runtime as the target runtime. [default: False]

Issues.Title: [release/3.1] Reset current_no_gc_region_info after leaving no gc region implicitly
Issues.Body:
Backport https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/73602.

## Customer Impact
Customers reported occasional `System.InvalidOperationException` with message `The NoGCRegion mode was already in progress` when calling `GC.TryStartNoGCRegion`. This is preventing them from using this optimization and impacting their cold start latencies.

## Testing
Customers have tried the fix on .NET 6 overnight and reported the exception never appears again. Meanwhile, there is an unpatched machine and observed 72 exceptions of the same type in the same time interval, proving this does fix the bug.

## Risk
Low. This only impact customer using `TryStartNoGCRegion`, and this is the right thing to do.

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Assembly version for DispatchProxy shim is too low resulting in duplicate types for DispatchProxy
Issues.Body:
Create a new `netstandard2.1` library.
Add a reference to `<PackageReference Include="System.Reflection.DispatchProxy" Version="4.7.1" />`
Try to use `DispatchProxy`

Expected: 
`DispatchProxy` is resolved from `netstandard.dll`

Actual:
```
error CS0433: The type 'DispatchProxy' exists in both 'System.Reflection.DispatchProxy, Version=4.0.6.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=b03f5f7f11d50a3a' and 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51'
```


Build contains conflict message:
```
Encountered conflict between 'CopyLocal:C:\src\dotnet\runtime\artifacts\bin\testPackages\cache\system.reflection.dispatchproxy\4.7.1\lib\netstandard2.0\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll' and 'Runtime:C:\Program Files\dotnet\packs\NETStandard.Library.Ref\2.1.0\ref\netstandard2.1\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll'. Choosing 'CopyLocal:C:\src\dotnet\runtime\artifacts\bin\testPackages\cache\system.reflection.dispatchproxy\4.7.1\lib\netstandard2.0\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll' because AssemblyVersion '4.0.6.0' is greater than '4.0.5.0'.
```

Other shims avoid this by setting the AssemblyVersion higher than that which was previously shipped.

Issues.Title: Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs
Issues.Body:
I'm completely perplexed.

I created a .Net Standard 2.0 library project.

I explicity added an AssemblyInfo.cs file, we need this because we use this utility to "stamp" our assemblies when we build them:

https://github.com/ygoe/NetRevisionTool

That utility is run as a pre/post build event and temporarily replaces placeholders in the AssemblyInformationalVersion attribute with runtime values (like repo folder name, commit ID, branch etc etc).

The completed assembly then has this info "burned" into it as we go forward.

.Net Standard is not working with this.

1. It seems to populatethe Package Version (in the project's Package section) with whatever we put into AssemblyInfo.cs for AssemblyInformationalVersion.
2. The version of the generated nuget package is always set as 1.0.0.

This is just mind blowing, is there no way we can do this seemingly simple operation any more if adopt .Net Standard?
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs " (#1775)

Issues.Title: Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions
Issues.Body:
I was looking through this repository to determine if .NET Standard 2.1 libraries support default interface methods - it looks like they do, given the presence of `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.RuntimeFeature.DefaultImplementationsOfInterfaces`, as well as my own experimenting in VS 2019. It seems I was mistaken when thinking that this was not the case, so I'm glad this repository is easily accessible to determine this.

But while doing this, I found it difficult to determine what commits were included in this particular .NET Standard version. I see that there's a tag `v2.1.0-prerelease.19126.1`, as well as branches `release/2.0.0`, `release/3.0`, and `release/3.0-preview9`. One of the machines I tested VS 2019 on had a `netstandard.dll` assembly, itself targeting .NETStandard v2.1.0, with AssemblyInformationalVersion `1.1.0+a5b5f2e1e369972c8ff1e2183979fab6099f52ef`; this commit is part of the `release/3.0` branch. However, another machine had a same-named assembly, targeting .NETCoreApp v3.0 and AssemblyInformationalVersion `3.0.0+4ac4c0367003fe3973a3648eb0715ddb0e3bbcea`, and I don't see that commit hash in this repository.

Additionally, [this blog post](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/the-future-of-net-standard/) states that 2.1 will be the last version, but there is another prerelease tag `v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1` and [on GitHub](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/releases/tag/v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1) it's labelled .NET 5.0 Preview 2.

So I have a few questions for understanding this repository:

1. Since .NET Standard 2.1 is released, are there plans to continue development in this repository for e.g. the shared BCL going forward with .NET 5+?
2. Are there multiple kinds of `netstandard.dll` for a single .NET Standard version? E.g. are there separate versions for .NET Framework to reference and for .NET Core / .NET 5+ to reference?
3. Do the tags / branch names in this repository correspond to a .NET Standard version or something else?
4. It looks like there are patch releases; are there patch versions of a single .NET Standard version?
5. Are there other repositories which are being used to create `netstandard.dll`?
6. Is there a way to determine, from the repository, which commit is the one used for a given release?

Thank you for your consideration.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions" (#1777)

Issues.Title: Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1
Issues.Body:
# Summary

.NET Standard version is not resolved correctly when a transitive dependency targets multiple .NET Standard versions.

# Environment

- Windows 10 (19042.746)
- .NET 5 SDK 5.0.201

# Minimal reproducible example
[bug.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/files/6209239/bug.zip)

This is a three-project solution:
- `TestProject1` targeting `netcoreapp3.1`
- `ClassProject1` targeting `netstandard2.0`
- `ClassProject2` targeting *both* `netstandard2.0` and `netstandard2.1`

The project dependency chain is: `TestProject1 -> ClassProject1 -> ClassProject2`

A method (`ClassProject2Test1`) on `ClassProject2` is hidden behind a `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.

# The issue

The unit test failed with a `MissingMethodException`

```
[xUnit.net 00:00:00.38]     TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [FAIL]
  Failed TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [2 ms]
  Error Message:
   System.MissingMethodException : Method not found: 'Void ClassLibrary2.Class2.Class2Test1()'.
  Stack Trace:
     at ClassLibrary1.Class1.Class1Test1()
   at TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1() in C:\Users\rex\source\netstandard-bug-repro\TestProject1\UnitTest1.cs:line 12
```

# Expected result

The compiler should have resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.0)*` 

# Actual result

The compiler resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.1)*` 

Which causes the exception because the offending method, `ClassProject2Test1`, was hidden by the `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1" (#1787)

Issues.Title: [BUG] [UWP] GetManifestResourceInfo doesn't work on UWP
Issues.Body:
# Summary
I was trying to access Embedded resources on UWP. Something like this

```C#
manifestResourceInfo = typeof(App).Assembly.GetManifestResourceInfo("UwpEmbeddedResourceBug.appsettings.json");
```
However, this doesn't work on UWP, even though it works like a charm on iOS for instance. 
Further, when you try to use this in UWP debug mode, it will return non-null `manifestResourceInfo`, however internally the `FileName` property will be null. But if you try to use the same on Release build, instead you will get an exception

```

Issues.Title: Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions
Issues.Body:
### Problem
There is a security vulnerability with the version of System.Text.RegularExpressions that is used by dotnet standard. The vulnerable version of System.Text.RegularExpressions is 4.3.0. Please see links below for the vulnerability documentation or discussion:

https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2019-0820
https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/111
https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2019-0820
https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-DOTNET-SYSTEMTEXTREGULAREXPRESSIONS-174708
https://www.whitesourcesoftware.com/vulnerability-database/CVE-2019-0820

The dotnet commit that fixed the vulnerability is https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/commit/19d4b1163d8a03dd90ff5fd1785eea6305112545

### Issue:
We use whitesource and it has caught this issue with high severity. We don't consume System.Text.RegularExpressions directly but packages that use this. Therefore as a transitive dependency due to NetStandard library, which is being used by several other dotnet packages like Castle Windsor, MassTransit etc., Once an update is available the others could followup and update.

### Code:

[The latest version 2.0.3 of Net standard ](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) still seem to be using System.Text.RegularExpressions version 4.3.0 as per https://github.com/dotnet/standard/blob/master/src/apicompat/netstandard/netstandard.depproj

### Fix
Please update[ library](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) targeting .netStandard 1.6 to update System.Text.RegularExpression package to latest secured version 4.3.1 to fix the security issue or kindly suggest alternatives.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions" (#1786)

Issues.Title: linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem
Issues.Body:
Hello,

I am currently using .NET core 2.2.x and EF Core. 2.2.6. I have a function that returns a List<Animal> from the database with no issue. It returns 11 results. However, when I try to use `.Where(p => p.DeletedAt.GetValueOrDefault(DateTime.Now) => DateTime.Now).ToList()`, it still should return 11 results, however it returns 0. I also eliminated the possibility that there is something wrong with my where clause (logic) because it works perfectly on 4.6.1 EF Core 2.2.6. Furthermore, I confirmed that it is only where I am comparing a nullable type using that function and I am guessing that I missed a thread someone opened on this issue. I am aware .NET core 2.2 is not LTS. I also thought this goes here because it's not AFAIK, an EF core issue but rather an Ienumerable/Linq issue.

Update: As it turns out your notion of `DateTime.Now` getting evaluated twice is true. To rectify that, I will now be using `DateTime.Now.Date`. This is odd because this exact code works on 4.6.1. You're probably right. SMH. Thank you @GrabYourPitchforks! You may now close.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem" (#1792)

Issues.Title: Strong name signature not valid
Issues.Body:
Since I've ported a ClickOnce application from .NET Framework 4.6.1 to .NET Standard 2.0, the message _"Strong assembly name signature not valid for **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**"_ appears when trying to install or update the application. So the next step was to verify the assembly strong name by using the [Strong Name Tool](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/tools/sn-exe-strong-name-tool) to make sure, that everything is fine, but:

```sh
> sn.exe -v Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll

Microsoft (R) .NET Framework Strong Name Utility Version 4.0.30319.0
Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. All rights reserved.

Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll is a delay-signed or test-signed assembly
```

Additional information:

- The assembly versions `161.46041.41` and `161.46367.54` ended up in the same result
- This issue looks very similar to [this](https://www.damirscorner.com/blog/posts/20140502-StrongNameValidationFailedSecurityException.html)
- @markingmyname / @olprod: The root package, which is required for [Server Management Objects (SMOs)](https://docs.microsoft.com/sql/relational-databases/server-management-objects-smo/overview-smo?view=sql-server-ver15), is:
  - [Microsoft.SqlServer.SqlManagementObjects](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SqlServer.SqlManagementObjects)
    - Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment
      - Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Authoring
        - **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**
- This issue appears on windows server machines but the software runs on different machines and I would like to avoid temporary workarounds such as editing the registry and activate the strong name bypass feature because of the forced validation on windows server machines

Issues.Title: System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings slow
Issues.Body:
_This issue has been moved from [a ticket on Developer Community](https://developercommunity2.visualstudio.com/t/SystemDrawingPrintingPrinterSettings-/890524)._ --- Hello I'm debugging a problem with the printer settings. Some calls are significant slower if the default printer is a network printer, even if I explicit set a local printer name. After studying referencesource I think I found the culprit. I call: var printerSettings = new System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings(); printerSettings.PrinterName = "LOCALPRINTER"; // the next call is slow if the OS default printer is a network printer var res = printerSettings.DefaultPageSettings.PrinterResolution Internally FastDeviceCapabilities is called. FastDeviceCapabilities calls GetOutputPort. But GetOutput port return the port of the default printer and not the port of the given printer! In addition, DeviceCapabilities is then called with a wrong combination of printer name and port, don't know if this could lead to additional problems. Resolution: GetOutputPort should return the port of the given printer and not accessing the default printer at all. Best Regards, Raphael --- ### Original Comments #### Raphael Affolter on 1/20/2020, 04:03 AM:

I forgot to mention: .Net Framework 4.6.1

#### Feedback Bot on 1/20/2020, 06:51 PM:

We have directed your feedback to the appropriate engineering team for further evaluation. The team will review the feedback and notify you about the next steps.

#### Raphael Affolter on 2/7/2020, 08:39 AM:

Because we print a lot, we really suffer from this performance penalty.

Also reading PaperSizes and PaperSources from the printer settings is slow caused by the same problem.

Could you please inform me about a possible fix?

Best Regards,

Raphael

#### Raphael Affolter on 2/7/2020, 10:33 AM:

In my opinion the fix is easy: replace GetOutputPort by OutputPort in the call to

FastDeviceCapabilities.

Done.

If so, in order for us to investigate further, please provide more information by recording your repro steps via the Visual Studio Feedback Tool (Help -> Send Feedback -> Report A Problem). Issues.Title: Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF
Issues.Body:
I'm working on converting a large WPF solution's projects to SDK style and ran into some issues.

The solution is large with multiple projects(old style) all targeting .net452 and some nugets(some made by me) installed, targeting both .net452 and .netstandard2.1 This all seems to work fine, somehow the nuget manages to install the correct version targeting .net452.

I have decided to slowly convert the projects inside the solution to SDK style targeting .net452 and .netstandard2.1 just like the nugets.

This is where the problem starts, one project was converted so far that is referenced by multiple other projects. Localy everything seems to build and run fine, however when Azure DevOps(VS version 2019) is used to build the solution there are 2 scenarios:

1. The famous error message is shown:

                "Error CS0012: The type 'Object' is defined in an assembly that is not referenced. You must add a reference to assembly 
                 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0"

2. It builds fine but on app launch it crashes with:

                 "Could not load file or assembly 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' 
                 or one of its dependencies. The system cannot find the file specified."

I'm suspecting that the problem is related to referencing the SDK project, it looks like that somehow it references the .netstandard2.1 instead of the .net452.

The reason this is my suspicion is that if targetframework is set to only .net452 on the referenced project everything works fine. Google has led me to two possible solutions to tell the project what framework to use from the reference:

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj"
                  AdditionalProperties="TargetFramework=net452">
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
and

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj">
      <SetTargetFramework>TargetFramework=net452</SetTargetFramework>
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <<Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
This doesn't look like it's doing anything and the problem still persists. At the moment I ran out of ideas and I'm here asking for help. Please let me know what I'm doing wrong or what else I can try.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF" (#1776)

**Context**

As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. Issues.Title: Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths
Issues.Body:
## Customer Impact

A customer reported in dotnet/runtime#71607 that decrypting RSA OAEP with SHA2 and a 3072-bit key on Linux resulted in a OAEP de-padding error, while other platforms were able to perform these operations successfully.

Investigation in to the issue led to uncover that RSA OAEP decryption that uses the managed implementation does not work with non-power-of-two keys because we do not slice a rented buffer accordingly. The current implementation only works because `CryptoPool.Rent` happens to give back power-of-two arrays which are exactly the same size as the key.

The fix is to slice the data to the correct size.

This does not affect dotnet/runtime because the managed implementation of RSA OAEP is no longer used for OpenSSL RSA decryption. This change was introduced in dotnet/runtime#50063.

## Testing

Unit tests were introduced to test RSA OAEP encryption with a 3072-bit RSA key. These tests will be forward-ported to dotnet/runtime.

## Risk

Minimal. The change is localized and understood that a `Slice` was missing.

Issues.Title: FSA diagnostics cache ignores analyzer filter changes on an unchanged project
Issues.Body:
### Description

Closed-file full-solution analysis (FSA) diagnostics can remain stale when compiler or analyzer diagnostic scopes change without changing the project snapshot. Fresh diagnostic pulls continue to return results computed using the previous analyzer filter.

Observed with the Roslyn language server bundled by dotnet/vscode-csharp:
- Version: `5.14.0-1.26552.2`
- Source revision: `eb07b178c241fad780d6fc947512f00bbdbd1dc4`
- Environment: VS Code on macOS, standalone C# extension (without C# Dev Kit)

The same cache implementation was also present in upstream `main` when investigated.

### Reproduction

Use a closed C# file containing both compiler and analyzer diagnostics, for example the [vscode-csharp diagnostics fixture](https://github.com/dotnet/vscode-csharp/blob/main/test/lsptoolshost/integrationTests/testAssets/slnWithCsproj/src/app/diagnostics.cs).

Keep `dotnet.backgroundAnalysis.analyzerDiagnosticsScope` set to `fullSolution` throughout:

1. Set `dotnet.backgroundAnalysis.compilerDiagnosticsScope` to `fullSolution`. Pull workspace diagnostics to populate the cache.
2. Change compiler scope to `none`, without editing any files, and pull diagnostics again.
3. Add and save whitespace in an unrelated C# file in the same project, then pull diagnostics again.
4. Change compiler scope back to `fullSolution`, without another edit, and pull diagnostics again.
5. Add and save another whitespace edit in the unrelated file, then pull diagnostics again.

The diagnostic target remained closed, and the language-server PID remained unchanged throughout the controlled reproduction.

| Step | Expected | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| Both scopes full solution | 5 diagnostics, including compiler warning `CS0219` | 5 |
| Compiler scope changed to none | 4 diagnostics, without `CS0219` | Still 5, including `CS0219` |
| Unrelated whitespace edit saved | 4 | 4 |
| Compiler scope changed back to full solution | 5, including `CS0219` | Still 4, missing `CS0219` |
| Second unrelated whitespace edit saved | 5 | 5 |

The five initial diagnostic codes were `CA1822`, `CS0219`, `IDE0005`, `IDE0059`, and `IDE0130`.

### Configuration and diagnostic freshness

This was reproduced while removing unnecessary server restarts from vscode-csharp integration tests. To rule out client timing and cached diagnostic collections, the experiment:

- Awaited forwarding of the final configuration notification.
- Sent `workspace/waitForAsyncOperations` after that notification to wait for server processing/background work.
- Requested full workspace diagnostic reports by omitting previous result IDs.
- Inspected newly returned reports through the normal language-client diagnostic pipeline, rather than relying only on existing VS Code diagnostic collections.

The returned full reports themselves contained the stale diagnostic set. Restarting the server, or changing the project snapshot through the unrelated edit, made the scopes take effect.

### Suspected root cause

[`AbstractWorkspaceDocumentDiagnosticSource.FullSolutionAnalysisDiagnosticSource`](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/eb07b178c241fad780d6fc947512f00bbdbd1dc4/src/LanguageServer/Protocol/Handler/Diagnostics/DiagnosticSources/AbstractWorkspaceDocumentDiagnosticSource.cs#L35) caches diagnostics using:

```csharp
ConditionalWeakTable<Project, AsyncLazy<ILookup<DocumentId, DiagnosticData>>>
```

The cached `AsyncLazy` captures `analyzerFilter` when it calls `GetDiagnosticsForIdsAsync`. However, `analyzerFilter` is not part of the cache identity. A subsequent source for the same `Project` instance but a different filter therefore reuses diagnostics calculated under the previous filter.

[`WorkspaceDocumentsAndProjectDiagnosticSourceProvider`](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/eb07b178c241fad780d6fc947512f00bbdbd1dc4/src/LanguageServer/Protocol/Handler/Diagnostics/DiagnosticSourceProviders/WorkspaceDocumentsAndProjectDiagnosticSourceProvider.cs) derives the filter from the current compiler/analyzer FSA scopes, so configuration changes can alter the filter without replacing the project instance.

The project-level diagnostic source does not use this particular cache; this report concerns closed-document FSA diagnostics.

### Suggested fix and regression coverage

Include `AnalyzerFilter` in the cache identity while preserving weak references to project instances and sharing cached computations across documents for the same project/filter.

Add regression tests that populate the real FSA source cache, then independently change compiler and analyzer scopes on the same project snapshot, in both directions, without file edits or server restarts. The existing [FSA on/off tests](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/eb07b178c241fad780d6fc947512f00bbdbd1dc4/src/LanguageServer/ProtocolUnitTests/Diagnostics/PullDiagnosticTests.cs#L2296) toggle both scopes together; they do not exercise a changed analyzer filter while FSA remains enabled.

### Impact

Users can continue seeing diagnostics that should have been disabled, or fail to see newly enabled diagnostics, until the project snapshot changes. This also currently prevents removing per-case server restarts from the closed-file diagnostics integration tests in dotnet/vscode-csharp.

Issues.Body:
Simplify compilation by removing the separate temporary-directory input and the plumbing needed to carry it through compiler entry points, MSBuild, and the build-server protocol.

Issues.Title: Use current source trees for definition locations after edits
Issues.Body:
Frozen partial semantics can return a symbol whose source span belongs to an older target document. The LSP handler resolves its document ID in the current solution and reports the wrong line or column after an edit.

Reject source locations whose trees differ from the current solution and retry full semantics. Unchanged target trees keep the frozen-semantic fast path from #72714.

The regression explicitly enables partial semantics, which production enables but test workspaces disable by default. It covers definition and type-definition, line and column movement, both LSP workspace modes, and C#/VB.

Validation:

- All 16 new cases fail without the fix and pass with it.
- All 72 definition tests pass, with no skips.
- The standalone LSP probe improves from 72/84 to 84/84 exact locations. Edited answers equal a clean restart.
- Affected builds pass with analyzers enabled. Whitespace and diff checks pass.

Issues.Title: Simplify ProjectData atomic write and temp directory routing
Issues.Body:
Alternative to https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/86210

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-dotnettools/issues/3715
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-dotnettools/issues/3541
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-dotnettools/issues/3564

### Motivation & Background

1. **Why `ReplaceOrMove` existed originally and why `File.Replace` failed (`#3541`, `#3715`)**
   - `ReplaceOrMove` (`File.Replace` → `File.Move` → `File.Replace`) was originally written when the task targeted `netstandard2.0`, which did not have `File.Move(string, string, bool overwrite)`.
   - On Windows, `File.Replace` calls Win32 `ReplaceFileW`, which opens the destination for metadata/attribute transfer and requires the replacement and destination paths to resolve on the same volume without cross-volume directory reparse points. This caused failures on ReFS volumes / Dev Drives ([microsoft/vscode-dotnettools#3541](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-dotnettools/issues/3541): `Access to the path is denied` / `Unable to remove the file to be replaced`) and when directories are redirected across volumes via Windows directory symbolic links ([microsoft/vscode-dotnettools#3715](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-dotnettools/issues/3715): `Unable to move the replacement file to the file to be replaced`).

2. **Why `File.Move(tempPath, outputPath, overwrite: true)` replaces `ReplaceOrMove`**
   - `Microsoft.NET.ProjectData.Tasks` now targets `$(NetRoslynSourceBuild)` (`net11.0`), where `File.Move(source, dest, overwrite: true)` is available directly.
   - `File.Move(..., overwrite: true)` uses `MoveFileExW` with `MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING` (and `MOVEFILE_COPY_ALLOWED`) on Windows and `rename(2)` (with cross-device fallback) on Unix, replacing the 3-step `ReplaceOrMove` helper in a single call.

3. **Why `IntermediateOutputPath` temp-file routing is only needed for project-folder `.lscache` writes (`#3564`)**
   - Staging the transient `.tmp` side-file under `$(IntermediateOutputPath)` (`obj/`) was introduced solely for source-tree hygiene when `.lscache` is written next to the `.csproj` (`EnableProjectDataInProjectFolder=true`), so transient `.tmp` files do not briefly appear in the source tree where Git, File Explorer, or file watchers can observe them.
   - For **user-folder caches** (`~/.local/share` / `%LOCALAPPDATA%`) and **inner-build `.slice` files** (which already live under `obj/`), routing the `.tmp` file through `$(IntermediateOutputPath)` is unnecessary. Worse, on Linux/macOS (such as DevContainers or Codespaces where `/workspaces/.../obj` and `~/.local/share/...` are on different mounts), `Path.GetPathRoot` returns `"/"` for both paths, causing the writer to stage the `.tmp` file in `obj/` and then attempt a cross-mount move into the user-folder cache ([microsoft/vscode-dotnettools#3564](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-dotnettools/issues/3564): `Invalid cross-device link`).
   - By omitting `IntermediateOutputPath` on `_WriteProjectDataSlice`, `_WriteProjectDataUserFolder`, and `_MergeProjectDataSlicesUserFolder`, transient `.tmp` files for slice and user-folder writes are staged directly beside `outputPath` on the destination filesystem.

4. **Improved failure diagnostics (`#3541`)**
   - Previously, `WriteProjectDataSliceTask` and `MergeProjectDataSlicesTask` logged only `ProjectFilePath` and `ex.Message` (producing warnings like `ProjectData: failed to write project-data file for Foo.csproj: Unable to remove the file to be replaced.` with no target path, exception type, or stack trace).
   - Both tasks now log `ResolvedOutputPath`, `ProjectFilePath`, and the full `ex` so any future I/O failure is immediately actionable.
 ###### Microsoft Reviewers: [Open in CodeFlow](https://microsoft.github.io/open-pr/?codeflow=https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/86327)

Issues.Title: Suboptimal codegen for `is` pattern: binary search prevents JIT from using a bit test
Issues.Body:
Since .NET 9, the JIT folds a chain of `==` comparisons against constants into a single `bt` with a constant mask. Roslyn lowers the equivalent `is` pattern to a binary search over the constants, so the JIT no longer sees that chain.

Repro: [compiler-explorer](https://compiler-explorer.com/z/4zPMoq1xP)

```csharp
public static int N_0(char c)
{
    if (c is < ' ' or > '~'
        or '"'
        or '\\'
        or '&'
        or '\''
        or '+'
        or '<'
        or '>'
        or '`')
        return 1;
    return 0;
}

public static int N_1(char c)
{
    if (c < ' ' || c > '~'
        || c == '"'
        || c == '\\'
        || c == '&'
        || c == '\''
        || c == '+'
        || c == '<'
        || c == '>'
        || c == '`')
        return 1;
    return 0;
}    
```

**`N_0` decompiled, the relevant part:**
```csharp
if (c <= '+')
{
    if (c <= '&')
    {
        if (c == '"' || c == '&')
            goto label_8;
    }
    else if (c == '\'' || c == '+')
        goto label_8;
}
else if (c <= '>')
{
    if (c == '<' || c == '>')
        goto label_8;
}
else if (c == '\\' || c == '`')
    goto label_8;
```

Both methods start with the same range check. The relevant part is what follows it.

**`N_0` (IL size: 84 bytes, code size: 89 bytes):**
```asm
G_M44197_IG05:
       cmp      eax, 43
       jle      SHORT G_M44197_IG07
       cmp      eax, 62
       jle      SHORT G_M44197_IG06
       cmp      eax, 92
       je       SHORT G_M44197_IG03
       cmp      eax, 96
       jne      SHORT G_M44197_IG09
       jmp      SHORT G_M44197_IG03
G_M44197_IG06:
       cmp      eax, 60
       je       SHORT G_M44197_IG03
       cmp      eax, 62
       je       SHORT G_M44197_IG03
       jmp      SHORT G_M44197_IG09
G_M44197_IG07:
       cmp      eax, 38
       jle      SHORT G_M44197_IG08
       cmp      eax, 39
       je       SHORT G_M44197_IG03
       cmp      eax, 43
       je       SHORT G_M44197_IG03
       jmp      SHORT G_M44197_IG09
G_M44197_IG08:
       cmp      eax, 34
       je       SHORT G_M44197_IG03
       cmp      eax, 38
       je       SHORT G_M44197_IG03
G_M44197_IG09:
       xor      eax, eax
       pop      rbp
       ret
```

**`N_1` (IL size: 54 bytes, code size: 52 bytes):**
```asm
G_M45220_IG05:
       add      eax, -34
       cmp      eax, 62
       ja       SHORT G_M45220_IG07
       mov      rcx, 0x4400000014000231
       bt       rcx, rax
       jb       SHORT G_M45220_IG03
G_M45220_IG07:
       xor      eax, eax
       pop      rbp
       ret
```

`N_0` does not get `bt` on .NET 9, 10 or 11 RC3, while `N_1` gets it on all three.

This is not specific to `is`. With the constants alone (no range checks), an `is` pattern, a `switch` statement and a switch expression all produce 77 bytes without `bt`, while the `||` chain produces 42 bytes.

The tree can also split a set that fits in one mask. For `is '"' or '\\' or '&' or '<' or '>' or '+'`, the JIT emits two `bt` instructions, one per half of the tree (68 bytes). The `||` chain gets one (42 bytes).

**Possible fix:** when all constants fit in a 64-bit window, Roslyn could emit a linear chain of `==` instead of the binary search. Larger sets would keep the binary search.

The trade-off is on runtimes without this optimization. On .NET 8, `N_1` is still smaller (68 vs 89 bytes), but it takes more comparisons on the worst path.

Issues.Title: Clear inherited MSBuildSDKsPath when launching dotnet
Issues.Body:
An inherited `MSBuildSDKsPath` can override the SDK selected by the child CLI.
For example, a path to the .NET 11 SDK can reach a .NET 10 CLI on `PATH`.
On macOS, I reproduced a `Canonical.csproj` restore stuck in a task-host connection after it loaded tasks from the .NET 11 SDK.

Clear this variable alongside `MSBUILD_EXE_PATH` and `MSBuildExtensionsPath` so the selected CLI resolves its own SDK. Add one regression through the existing helper, without a new product test hook.

A controlled environment comparison isolates the SDK-path override as the trigger. The regression fails against the original helper, and the previously stalled miscellaneous-file cases complete with the fix.

Issues.Title: Specify that ProjectData tasks are .NET
Issues.Body:
These tasks are built only for modern .NET, so if they're triggered in
an MSBuild.exe-hosted build, they emit a warning

    MSBUILD : warning : The custom task 'Microsoft.NET.ProjectData.Tasks' required a fallback to out-of-process execution because the UsingTask definition does not specify the correct Runtime and Architecture. This reduces build performance. Update the UsingTask element to explicitly specify Runtime and Architecture attributes (e.g., Runtime="CLR4" Architecture="x64") or use TaskFactory="TaskHostFactory".

That's because MSBuild detects the target framework of the DLL and runs
it compatibly--but the warning is annoying. Specifying that the task
run in a modern .NET TaskHost codifies that behavior without the perf
hit of failing to load the task, analyzing why, and retrying in the
right process.

Issues.Title: File-based apps: go-to-definition for `#:include`, `#:project`, and `#:ref` directives
Issues.Body:
Replacement for #84756 which got stale.

This now uses just the workspaces Project representation to find navigation targets, and the file-based apps helpers to interpret the directives.

`#:include Files/**/*.cs` and similar globs are supported. Multiple navigation targets are returned where applicable.

Following cases are not supported:
- `#:include MyFile?.cs`. `?` apparently is a pattern matching a single character. It works in msbuild but is not supported by the globbing library, at least not the way I am using it, and seems uncommon/unimportant.
- `#:include $(MyProperty)/File.cs`. This also seems uncommon in practice but we could consider a future improvement to have the project system expand these before trying to navigate.
- `#:include File1.cs;File2.cs`. Also uncommon.

This adds a package reference to workspaces layer, so I created a test insertion: https://dev.azure.com/devdiv/DevDiv/_git/VS/pullrequest/803246

This feature is not expected to work in VS, so, no new DLL loads are expected in VS. But the insertion should help us verify that the new package reference doesn't break product construction or deployment.

Issues.Title: Blazor event debounce and throttling prototype
Issues.Body:
## Summary

This PR is the Razor compiler half of a prototype for Blazor event debouncing and throttling (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/10522), paired with the runtime change in https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70311.

## Architecture

The implementation extends the existing `@on{EVENT}:preventDefault` and `@on{EVENT}:stopPropagation` directive attribute parameter pipeline:

1. **Tag helper production (`EventHandlerTagHelperProducer`):** Following the existing `preventDefault` and `stopPropagation` rules, `EventHandlerTagHelperProducer` registers `:debounce` and `:throttle` (`int` milliseconds) tag matching rules and `BoundAttributeParameter` descriptors on event handler tag helpers, and stores the `[EventHandler]` attribute's `EventThrottleMode` in `EventHandlerMetadata`.
2. **IR lowering and code generation (`ComponentEventHandlerLoweringPass` & `ComponentNodeWriter`):** Just as `preventDefault` and `stopPropagation` lower to `ComponentAttributeIntermediateNode` calls to `AddEventPreventDefaultAttribute` and `AddEventStopPropagationAttribute`, `:debounce` and `:throttle` lower to `AddEventDebounceAttribute` and `AddEventThrottleAttribute` (appending `EventThrottleMode.LeadingAndTrailing` when specified in `EventHandlerMetadata`). Because `ComponentEventHandlerLoweringPass` runs before `ComponentBindLoweringPass`, `@bind` with `@bind:event="oninput"` and `@oninput:debounce="300"` works automatically.
3. **Diagnostics (`ComponentDiagnosticFactory`):** Following the existing duplicate and mutually exclusive `@bind` parameter diagnostics (such as `RZ10018`), the pass reports `RZ10031` when `:debounce` and `:throttle` are combined on the same event and `RZ10032` when used as a minimized attribute without an interval value.

Issues.Title: Fix nullable annotation warning from nameof emission for a generic component parameter
Issues.Body:
Fixes dotnet/aspnetcore#69947.

Using a generic component with a nullable type argument together with another parameter:

```razor
<MyComponent T="string?" Param="1" />
```

makes the compiler emit the parameter name as `nameof(global::...MyComponent<string?>.Param)`. In `WriteComponentAttributeName` the property name goes through a source-mapped pragma, which carries `#nullable restore`, but the containing type is written raw, so `string?` lands in a `#nullable disable` region and the caller's generated code warns CS8669.

This change writes the containing type between `#nullable restore` and `#nullable disable` when its text contains a nullable annotation and nullability enforcement is not suppressed, following the pattern `InjectTargetExtension` already uses for `@inject`. Types without an annotation emit exactly as before.

Tests: adds `AddComponentParameter_WithNameof_GenericComponent_NullableTypeArgument` with baselines. The full `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Razor.Language` test project passes with no other baseline changes: 4,649 passed, 0 failed, on both net10.0 and net472.

Related: dotnet/roslyn#85648 reports the same warning through `@bind`. This change covers the `AddComponentParameter` nameof path; I haven't verified it against the `@bind` scenario.

Issues.Title: Terminate multiline C# attribute values when formatting Razor
Issues.Body:
Fixes #86306 (the bound case described in [this comment](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/86306#issuecomment-6632823628)).

In `VisitMultilineCSharpExpressionLiteral`, the last line of a multiline expression only got a `;` for block-bodied lambdas. A C# expression that is the whole value of a component or directive attribute was left unterminated:

```razor
<button @onclick="() => Show(1,
                  2)"
   class="x">y</button>
```

Roslyn then read the next attribute line as part of the expression, and `class="x"` landed one level too shallow in every attribute indent style. The `@onclick="@(() => …)"` form was already right. This extends the `emitSemiColon` condition to `node.Parent is MarkupTagHelperAttributeValueSyntax`, still only when the line continues past the expression.

Tests:
- New in `RazorFormatterTest`: `TryFormatAsync_MultilineDirectiveAttributeLambda`, plus `_IndentByOne` and `_IndentByTwo`.
- New in `DocumentFormattingTest`: `MultilineLambdaInDirectiveAttribute_MovesWithTag`, plus `_IndentByOne` and `_IndentByTwo`.
- The expected output for each test is what the `@(` form produces on `main`. Without the new condition, all 6 fail.
- `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Razor.DotNetFormat.UnitTests` passes, 35 of 35.
- The cohosting formatting tests pass, 652 passed and 1 skipped, including the multiline lambda tests from #84121.

Not verified: the hand-written `htmlFormatted` values against WebTools, which only runs on .NET Framework, and the net472 VS test project.

Issues.Title: Close Html elements whose end tag isn't first on a line in Razor formatting
Issues.Body: Fixes #86304 `CSharpDocumentGenerator` turns an element that causes indentation into a `{` (in `VisitStartTag`) and its end tag into a `}` (in `VisitEndTag`). But `Generate()` only visits the first node on each line, so an end tag later in a line never emitted its `}`. Everything after it was indented one level too deep, to the end of the file. A Razor comment in front of the end tag is one way to get there. `text `, `a `, `@DateTime.Now ` and ` ` all fail the same way. The fix: - **Track the open braces:** the generator records the positions of start tags it emitted `{` for. - **Emit the missing braces:** after visiting a line, it emits a `}` for each later end tag in that line whose start tag is in that set. The braces go on lines after the current one, which keeps the line indented as content of the element. Those lines are then skipped when mapping back. - **Skip by count:** the C# formatter splits `}}` onto separate lines, so `LineInfo.SkipNextLine` (bool) becomes `SkipNextLines` (int). The generator is shared, so the cohosted path has the same bug whenever the Html formatter leaves the end tag on that line. `DocumentFormattingTest.EndTagAfterRazorCommentOnSameLine` covers it. Tests: - New: `RazorFormatterTest.TryFormatAsync_EndTagAfterRazorCommentOnSameLine`, `TryFormatAsync_MultipleEndTagsAfterRazorCommentOnSameLine` (`@* note *@ `), and `DocumentFormattingTest.EndTagAfterRazorCommentOnSameLine`. - Without the new call, all three fail. With `iFormatted++` instead of `+= SkipNextLines`, the multiple-end-tags test fails. - `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Razor.DotNetFormat.UnitTests` passes, 34 of 34. - The cohosting formatting tests pass, 650 passed and 1 skipped. They were run through `Microsoft.VisualStudioCode.RazorExtension.UnitTests` on macOS. Two things I couldn't check. The cohost test passes `validateHtmlFormattedMatchesWebTools: false` (that check only runs on .NET Framework), and I haven't run the net472-only VS test project. Not covered here: a start tag later in a line (`text ` … ``) has the mirror-image problem for its contents. Seen in the wild in dotnet/eShop `src/HybridApp/Components/Layout/HeaderBar.razor`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ###### Microsoft Reviewers: [Open in CodeFlow](https://microsoft.github.io/open-pr/?codeflow=https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/86308)

Issues.Title: Indent Razor by indent_size under dotnet format
Issues.Body:
Fixes #86303

The formatting engine indents by `FormattingEngineOptions.TabSize` columns per level, as an LSP client's `tabSize`. The `dotnet format` entry point (`RazorFormatter.GetFormattingOptions`) filled it from `tab_width`, so `indent_size` was ignored. With `indent_size = 2` and `tab_width = 4`, both the markup and the C# in `@code` blocks were indented by 4. `GetResolvedCSharpSyntaxFormattingOptions` sets `IndentationSize` from the same value.

With spaces, this passes `indent_size`. With tabs, a level is one tab, so it keeps `tab_width`. That matters for how aligned columns are written: `TryFormatAsync_IndentsByTabsUsingOneTabPerLevel` aligns an attribute, and passing `indent_size` there would write four tabs where two tabs and two spaces are right at `tab_width = 4`.

Only the `dotnet format` entry point changes; the cohosted path still takes `tabSize` from the client.

Tests: the two new tests in `RazorFormatterTest`. The spaces test fails without the fix, and the tabs test fails with the simpler `TabSize = IndentationSize`. `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Razor.DotNetFormat.UnitTests` passes, 34 of 34.

I found this while comparing a Razor formatter of my own against this one through the `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Razor.DotNetFormat` package.

Issues.Title: Avoid no-op CI investigator environment stalls and oversized job outputs
Issues.Body:
## Summary

The CI Investigator stopped filing issues, seemingly because of a GitHub incident:
https://www.githubstatus.com/incidents/dqn46wtvbdzv
https://www.githubstatus.com/incidents/djlmxz2zd0j7

In this incident, actions workflows had a 'loss of run state' bug, which causes jobs to permanently block and never proceed past 'pre-activation'. That's exactly what happened with our workflow, and it is within the specified outage windows:

The problematic run was:  https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/37442110088

This PR fixes two issues to try to reduce the potential for this problem given any future outage:
- GitHub's 1 MB job-output channel blocked sending 'evidence' including failed test results for large failure outputs, which prevented the investigator from running. 

- Empty/skipped runs used to request the protected PAT environment, which was wasteful and could block the queue unnecessarily.

- The workflow-wide concurrency lock let one stuck run block every later investigation. Only the `collect` job (which owns the processed-build checkpoint) is now serialized; other jobs run per-run, so a stuck admission blocks only its own run. Issues now record failure and mechanism fingerprints for cross-run deduplication; rare duplicates are possible when two runs investigate the same failure concurrently.

- gh-aw v0.89 stopped exporting the safe-output temporary ID map, so a run that filed several issues dispatched Issue Monster only for the first. The dispatcher now also finds this run's open `live-build-incident` issues by gh-aw's provenance marker. Verified e2e in the fork: https://github.com/nagilson/sdk/actions/runs/41937928505 filed 3 issues and dispatched Issue Monster for all 3.

Alternatives:
- We could make a pipeline that clears out the queue, though I avoided doing so because it seems like hacky extra cost to workaround a GH infra issue.

Issues.Title: Forward help after dotnetup dotnet commands
Issues.Body:
Fixes #56952.

First identified while investigating #56244; that issue's `dotnet-format.dll` path error is a separate NativeAOT formatter-forwarding bug.

## Change

`dotnetup dotnet <command> ...` now treats arguments after the dotnet command as passthrough arguments. This forwards command help such as:

```console
dotnetup dotnet format --help
```

instead of showing help for dotnetup's `dotnet` wrapper.

`dotnetup dotnet --help` still shows wrapper help. To request the root `dotnet` help, use:

```console
dotnetup dotnet -- --help
```

## User-visible behavior

Help options after a forwarded dotnet command now reach `dotnet` instead of dotnetup.

## Validation

- `scripts\RunTests.cs` for `dotnetup.Tests` with parser, help, and `DotnetCommandTests` filters: 186 passed, 0 failed.
- Built dotnetup end to end:
  - `dotnetup dotnet format --help` prints formatter help.
  - `dotnetup dotnet --help` prints wrapper help.

Issues.Title: dotnetup dotnet intercepts --help instead of forwarding it
Issues.Body:
### Description

`dotnetup dotnet` should forward arguments to the dotnetup-managed `dotnet` executable, but dotnetup intercepts `--help` after the forwarded command name.

This was first identified while investigating #56244. That issue's `dotnet-format.dll` path error is a separate NativeAOT formatter-forwarding bug; this issue tracks only dotnetup's argument handling.

### Repro

In a directory with no `global.json`:

```console
dotnetup dotnet format --help
```

### Expected

The `dotnet format` help, as produced by:

```console
dotnet format --help
```

### Actual

dotnetup prints help for its own `dotnet` wrapper command:

```text
Description:
  Run a command using the dotnetup-managed dotnet installation.

Usage:
  dotnetup dotnet [options] [[--] <additional arguments>...]]
```

### Workaround

Use the separator so dotnetup forwards `--help`:

```console
dotnetup dotnet -- format --help
```

### Likely cause

The `dotnet` command uses `TreatUnmatchedTokensAsErrors = false` and forwards `ParseResult.UnmatchedTokens`, but `--help` is still recognized by System.CommandLine as dotnetup's help option before `DotnetCommand` runs:

- [`DotnetCommandParser`](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/a98e2d0757a/src/Installer/dotnetup.Library/Commands/Dotnet/DotnetCommandParser.cs)
- [`DotnetCommand`](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/a98e2d0757a/src/Installer/dotnetup.Library/Commands/Dotnet/DotnetCommand.cs)

Verified with the locally built dotnetup at `a98e2d0757a` on Windows.

Issues.Title: [release/10.0.1xx] Preserve existing test runners when creating MTP projects
Issues.Body:
## Description

Backport of #56945 to `release/10.0.1xx`. This is a manual backport of the requested open PR snapshot, not a request to merge the source PR.

Both source commits are included:

- `01bcaf6e709cd97603ef864c6dbce4ca03e603a6`: overwrite protection.
- `1c371ea1e1f2cfee50c97955bd84ab43d00ef71c`: case-equivalent runner correction.

The source remains open at the second commit. The refreshed target base is `950f4b138bfcc4faa9250f945554a8353cb5ca82`. The shared processor exactly matches the source-head blob.

Add `allowPropertyOverwrite` (default `true`) and `ignorePropertyValueCase` (default `false`) to the JSON post-action. The latter uses ordinal case-insensitive comparison only for scalar strings when overwriting is disabled. Conflicting existing values remain untouched and produce the localized diagnostic; matching runner values retain their stored casing. Generic comparison defaults, nested JSON, property names, and value types remain strict.

### Branch-specific adaptations

- Update only the four existing MTP post-actions in `Microsoft.DotNet.Common.ProjectTemplates.10.0`: MSTest C#/F#/VB and Playwright MSTest C#. Do not add a version-11 tree or MTP support to NUnit/xUnit templates.
- Preserve xUnit and this branch's `ToolsetInfo.CurrentTargetFramework` API. Use argument arrays/lists accepted by the branch's StyleCop version, without disabling analyzers.
- The branch's existing CLI runner parser rejects trailing commas in `global.json`; product fixtures retain comments/unrelated settings but use accepted JSON. Standalone post-action unit coverage still verifies byte-for-byte preservation of commented/trailing-comma JSON on conflicts. The parser itself is unchanged.
- Generate the resource accessor and XLIFF updates with supported MSBuild tasks. Servicing documentation makes no claim about a first shipping patch version.

## Customer Impact

Creating an MTP project no longer silently switches an ancestor VSTest runner and breaks existing projects in that scope. Protected template post-actions retain `continueOnError`: creation exits 0 after a conflict diagnostic, and the user must reconcile the runner choice.

Plain `dotnet new mstest` still defaults to VSTest. Missing runner settings still receive automatic MTP setup. This does not introduce mixed-runner solution support.

## Regression?

The overwrite behavior already exists on this servicing branch. With SDK `10.0.113` and the branch's MSTest/MSTest.Sdk `4.0.1` templates, both project styles ran an existing VSTest test successfully (exit 0, one passing test), then MTP project creation exited 0 while changing the runner, and the existing project subsequently failed with exit 1 and the incompatible-runner diagnostic.

## Risk

The template opt-ins and processor must ship together: older hosts ignore the new arguments. Other JSON post-action authors retain the existing overwrite/default comparison behavior.

No dependency upgrades, framework migrations, workflow changes, new audit suppression, or new analyzer suppression are included. Generated localization is included.

## Testing

The full branch SDK/layout build passed with **0 warnings and 0 errors**, producing `dotnet-sdk-10.0.115-dev-win-x64.zip`.

Validation runs the actual `artifacts\bin\redist\Debug\dotnet-installer` shipping layout, not the parent's .NET 12 layout or the stage-zero SDK. Its inventory is SDK **10.0.115-dev**, runtime **10.0.15**, common templates **10.0.115-dev**, and MSTest/MSTest.Sdk **4.0.1**.

- **48/48** focused JSON post-action unit cases passed, no skips.
- **22/22** product/integration cases passed, no skips: all existing template conflicts, missing/canonical/lowercase/mixed-case MTP settings, default VSTest, and real `dotnet test` execution in both supported MSTest project styles.
- Existing VSTest projects remain runnable after guarded MTP creation; compatible MTP projects retain runner casing and execute one passing test. Intentionally incompatible runner selection is also asserted to fail.

### Reproduction commands

Run from the repository root with the x64 Visual Studio developer environment. The verified native toolchain was VS 18 Insiders/MSVC 14.52.37025 and Windows SDK 10.0.26100.0. Restore the process-local Windows paths after entering the developer shell:

```powershell
Import-Module 'C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\18\Insiders\Common7\Tools\Microsoft.VisualStudio.DevShell.dll'
Enter-VsDevShell -VsInstallPath 'C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\18\Insiders' -SkipAutomaticLocation -DevCmdArguments '-arch=x64 -host_arch=x64'
$env:PATH = "C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0;C:\Windows\System32;$env:PATH"
$env:PATHEXT = '.COM;.EXE;.BAT;.CMD'
$sdk = 'C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10'
$v = '10.0.26100.0'
$env:WindowsSdkDir = "$sdk\"
$env:WindowsSDKVersion = "$v\"
$env:INCLUDE = "$sdk\Include\$v\ucrt;$sdk\Include\$v\shared;$sdk\Include\$v\um;$sdk\Include\$v\winrt;$sdk\Include\$v\cppwinrt;$env:INCLUDE"
$env:LIB = "$sdk\Lib\$v\ucrt\x64;$sdk\Lib\$v\um\x64;$env:LIB"
$env:DOTNET_ADD_GLOBAL_TOOLS_TO_PATH = '0'
.\build.cmd /bl /v:minimal /nr:false /p:IlcUseEnvironmentalTools=true
```

The build used explicit Windows SDK `ucrt/shared/um/winrt/cppwinrt` INCLUDE paths and `ucrt\x64`/`um\x64` LIB paths. The declared 10.0.15 runtime was provisioned from its exact NuGet runtime package for bootstrap unit execution because the public runtime archives returned 404; no runtime-version override was used.

Pin a test-directory SDK boundary so the repository's stage-zero `global.json` cannot select SDK 10.0.113. Use the branch's existing directory-build isolation files and its supported test-assets environment setting:

```powershell
$root = (Get-Location).Path
$run = Join-Path $root 'artifacts\tmp\net10-shipping-validation'
$shippingRoot = Join-Path $root 'artifacts\bin\redist\Debug\dotnet-installer'
$shippingHost = Join-Path $shippingRoot 'dotnet.exe'
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $run -Force | Out-Null
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path artifacts\log\net10-backport-validation -Force | Out-Null
Copy-Item test\dotnet-new.IntegrationTests\TestDirectoryBuildFiles\Directory.Build.props $run
Copy-Item test\dotnet-new.IntegrationTests\TestDirectoryBuildFiles\Directory.Build.targets $run
Copy-Item NuGet.config $run
'{"sdk":{"version":"10.0.115-dev","allowPrerelease":true}}' | Set-Content (Join-Path $run 'global.json')
$env:DOTNET_SDK_TEST_ASSETS_DIRECTORY = Join-Path $root 'test\TestAssets'
$env:DOTNET_ROOT = $shippingRoot
$env:DOTNET_HOST_PATH = $shippingHost
$env:DOTNET_MSBUILD_SDK_RESOLVER_CLI_DIR = $shippingRoot
$env:DOTNET_TEST_RUNNER = ''
$env:DOTNET_MULTILEVEL_LOOKUP = '0'
$env:MSBUILDDISABLENODEREUSE = '1'

.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe exec artifacts\bin\Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Cli.UnitTests\Debug\Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Cli.UnitTests.dll -class 'Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Cli.UnitTests.PostActionTests.AddJsonPropertyPostActionTests' -dotnetPath $shippingHost -testExecutionDirectory $run -sdkVersion 10.0.115-dev -xml artifacts\log\net10-backport-validation\net10-post-action-shipping.xml -nologo
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe exec artifacts\bin\dotnet-new.IntegrationTests\Debug\dotnet-new.IntegrationTests.dll -method '*ProjectTemplate_MtpRunner*' -method '*MtpProjectCreation*' -method '*MSTestProjectTemplate_UsesVSTestByDefault*' -dotnetPath $shippingHost -testExecutionDirectory $run -sdkVersion 10.0.115-dev -xml artifacts\log\net10-backport-validation\net10-mtp-integration.xml -nologo
```

The final test-source rebuilds also passed without warnings:

```powershell
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe build test\Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Cli.UnitTests\Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Cli.UnitTests.csproj --no-restore -v:minimal -nr:false -p:BuildTestPackages=false

```

XML, command logs, SDK/runtime inventory, packaged-template identity, and baseline results are retained locally under `artifacts\log\net10-backport-validation`; the successful full-build binlog is `artifacts\log\net10-backport-successful-build.binlog`.

### Limits and CI

The target already contains `NoWarn=NU1903` in `Directory.Build.props`; this backport does not change that inherited setting or add suppression. The source PR's Build Analysis check remains failed, with previously observed unrelated compiler-package audit diagnostics; this work does not claim to fix that check. This backport's GitHub CI remains a separate check after publication.

No PR was merged and Agent merge was not enabled.

Issues.Title: [release/11.0.1xx] Preserve existing test runners when creating MTP projects
Issues.Body:
Backport of #56945.

## Provenance and scope

Manual backport of the requested current, still-open source PR to `release/11.0.1xx`. Both source commits are included:

- `01bcaf6e709cd97603ef864c6dbce4ca03e603a6` - overwrite protection.
- `1c371ea1e1f2cfee50c97955bd84ab43d00ef71c` - case-equivalent MTP runner correction.

Validated release base: `782b84af1a2035cf220bbe7a405a7a2c4b82aa5a`.
Backport commit: `7c0e33b7844c3a14e559f254d86fe6aa725890d2`.
The source/main PR is unchanged. This is not the automated `/backport` workflow, which requires a merged source PR.

## Behavior and branch adaptations

The shared JSON post-action and all ten existing MTP global.json post-actions ship together. `allowPropertyOverwrite` defaults to `true`; `ignorePropertyValueCase` defaults to `false` and only enables ordinal case-insensitive scalar-string comparison when overwrite protection is selected. Conflicts preserve the exact file and report a localized diagnostic; compatible runner values retain their stored casing. Generic JSON defaults, nested objects/arrays, and value types remain strict.

Keep this branch's MSTest harness, `ToolsetInfo.CurrentTargetFramework` API, `Microsoft.DotNet.Common.ProjectTemplates.11.0` paths, and MSTest/MSTest.Sdk **4.5.2**. No test migration, dependency upgrade, additional MTP-enabled template, audit suppression, or CI bypass is included. The designer was generated with bootstrap MSBuild's `GenerateResource` task; the full repository build regenerated all 13 XLF files.

The source regressions are carried over, with additional default-VSTest and strict nested-array/boolean-versus-string coverage. Project creation still exits 0 through the existing `continueOnError` contract after a conflict. Plain MSTest creation still defaults to VSTest, and absent runner settings still receive automatic MTP setup. This does not introduce mixed-runner solution support. Servicing documentation requires an updated host and template package without inventing a first shipping patch version.

## Validation

| Component | Version / result |
| --- | --- |
| Bootstrap SDK | `11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105` |
| Built shipping SDK | `11.0.100-dev`; this branch's layout, not the parent's .NET 12 layout |
| Runtime / NativeAOT compiler | `11.0.0`; native `dotnet-aot.dll` produced |
| Shipped common-project templates | `Microsoft.DotNet.Common.ProjectTemplates.11.0`, package `11.0.100-dev`; all ten guarded post-actions checked inside the nupkg |
| Generated MSTest / MSTest.Sdk projects | `4.5.2`, both supported project styles targeting `net11.0` |
| Repository test harness | Branch-pinned `MSTest.Sdk` `4.5.0-preview.26477.3` |
| Full SDK/layout/NativeAOT build | Exit 0, 0 errors, 12 unsuppressed baseline audit warnings |
| JSON post-action unit cases | 47 passed, 0 failed/skipped |
| Focused template/product integration cases | 28 passed, 0 failed/skipped |
| Real shipped-template matrix | 10 scenarios; 30 successful `dotnet test` commands and 32 passing test executions; both historical runner-mutation controls correctly exit 1 |

The real matrix covers explicit VSTest conflicts, VSTest defaults, missing configuration, canonical/lowercase/mixed-case MTP settings, continued execution of existing and compatible new projects, and two-project solutions in both MSTest project styles. For each solution, both per-module TRX reports and the merged TRX were checked for exact counts and identical execution-ID unions, rather than double-counting merged artifacts.

Exact repository commands, after process-local x64 VS DevShell initialization with MSVC `14.52.37025` and Windows SDK `10.0.26100.0` headers/libraries:

```powershell
$env:DOTNET_ADD_GLOBAL_TOOLS_TO_PATH = '0'
$env:MSBUILDDISABLENODEREUSE = '1'
$env:DOTNET_CLI_USE_MSBUILD_SERVER = '0'
# PATH also includes C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0 for the runtime installer.
.\eng\build.ps1 /bl:artifacts\log\net11-backport-build.binlog /v:minimal /nr:false /p:IlcUseEnvironmentalTools=true
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe .github\skills\targeted-test\scripts\RunTargetedTests.cs -- --project test\Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Cli.UnitTests\Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Cli.UnitTests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~AddJsonPropertyPostActionTests"
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe .github\skills\targeted-test\scripts\RunTargetedTests.cs -- --project test\dotnet-new.IntegrationTests\dotnet-new.IntegrationTests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ProjectTemplate_MtpRunner|FullyQualifiedName~MtpProjectCreation|FullyQualifiedName~ProjectTemplate_DefaultRunnerRemainsVSTest"
```

Standalone shipping commands use `artifacts\bin\redist\Debug\dotnet\dotnet.exe`, a clean custom hive and isolated repository per scenario, and the shipped nupkg rather than installing source templates. The retained `evidence.json` records every exact working directory, argument vector, expected/actual exit code, and TRX path for all 57 commands. `DOTNET_TEST_RUNNER` is cleared so global.json is authoritative; first-run banners/certificate generation are disabled without hiding diagnostics.

Retained local diagnostics:

- `artifacts\log\net11-backport-build.binlog`
- `artifacts\log\targeted-tests\Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Cli.UnitTests\20261105-165159-123216\`
- `artifacts\log\targeted-tests\dotnet-new.IntegrationTests\20261105-165342-113824\`
- `artifacts\log\net11-shipping-20261105-170350\evidence.json` and its stdout/stderr/TRX/binlog artifacts

## Limits

The full build reports existing `NU1902`/`NU1903` findings for `System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs` 8.0.1 in compatibility projects and `NU1902` findings for `MessagePack` 3.1.8 in unrelated test projects. These dependencies and audit settings are unchanged; this backport does not resolve those baseline findings. An initial bootstrap attempt failed because `powershell.exe` was missing from PATH; adding the standard Windows PowerShell directory fixed it without bypassing installation or native compilation.

CI and servicing review remain required. No merge or Agent merge was requested or enabled.

Issues.Title: Preserve existing test runners when creating MTP projects
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Creating an MTP test project currently overwrites an explicitly configured ancestor `global.json` runner from VSTest to Microsoft.Testing.Platform. This silently changes the repository-wide runner selection and causes existing VSTest projects to fail `dotnet test`.

- Add `allowPropertyOverwrite` to the shared JSON post-action, retaining the existing `true` default for compatibility. Add opt-in `ignorePropertyValueCase` for scalar strings, defaulting to `false`.
- Enable overwrite protection and ordinal case-insensitive runner matching in all ten affected MSTest, Playwright MSTest, NUnit, and xUnit v3 template configurations. Conflicting values leave the file unchanged and produce a localized diagnostic; case-equivalent MTP values retain their existing casing.
- Keep generic JSON comparisons case-sensitive by default, without case-folding nested JSON or conflating value types. Cover ancestor configuration, compatible setup, and continued execution of existing projects in both MSTest project styles. Update the post-action documentation and generated localized resources.

## Compatibility and servicing

Project creation retains its existing `continueOnError` behavior and exits 0 after reporting a conflict; the user must reconcile the runner choice. Matching runners and missing runner settings still support automatic MTP setup. Plain `dotnet new mstest` continues to default to VSTest. This does not introduce mixed-runner solution support.

The same vulnerable source is present on `release/10.0.1xx` and `release/11.0.1xx`. Servicing requires both the processor and template changes because older hosts ignore the new arguments. This PR changes `main` only.

## Validation

The full SDK layout, including Native AOT, built successfully with zero warnings and errors. All 45 focused unit cases and 37 product/integration cases passed.

The composed scenarios use the built `12.0.100-dev` SDK and generated MSTest/MSTest.Sdk 4.4.0 projects. They reproduce the historical VSTest failure with exit 1 after runner mutation, then verify exit 0 and one passing test after guarded MTP project creation. Lowercase and mixed-case MTP setup regressions failed on the previous head and pass on the corrected layout, with compatible projects continuing to execute.

Commands used with the x64 Visual Studio developer environment and Windows SDK 10.0.26100.0 headers/libraries configured:

```powershell
$env:DOTNET_ADD_GLOBAL_TOOLS_TO_PATH = '0'
.\eng\build.ps1 /bl /v:minimal /nr:false /p:IlcUseEnvironmentalTools=true
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe scripts\RunTests.cs -- --project test\Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Cli.UnitTests\Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Cli.UnitTests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~AddJsonPropertyPostActionTests" --skip-redist-check
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe scripts\RunTests.cs -- --project test\dotnet-new.IntegrationTests\dotnet-new.IntegrationTests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ProjectTemplate_MtpRunner|FullyQualifiedName~MtpProjectCreation|FullyQualifiedName~ProjectTemplate_CanTargetSdkFrameworkWithoutRestore"
```

TRX and build binlog diagnostics are retained locally under `artifacts\log\test-runs\Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Cli.UnitTests\20261105-144041-105492` and `artifacts\log\test-runs\dotnet-new.IntegrationTests\20261105-144644-119276`.

Context: [microsoft/WindowsAppSDK#6885](https://github.com/microsoft/WindowsAppSDK/pull/6885#discussion_r4408283704).

Issues.Title: Fix issue triage team assignment and notifications
Issues.Body:
The [triage comment on #56930](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56930#issuecomment-6627157948) identified `@dotnet/dotnet-testing`, but left the issue unassigned and rendered the team handle as code instead of a live mention.

This change fixes both routing paths:

- Replace the stale `dotnet-testing-admin` snapshot with the verified members of the exact `dotnet-testing` team named by CODEOWNERS, restoring individual assignment candidates.
- Explicitly allow fully qualified CODEOWNERS team handles through `safe-outputs.mentions.allowed`. `allowed-teams` expands individual member mentions, not team handles, and its membership API calls fail without `read:org`.
- Keep team mentions raw even when no individual can be assigned, and document the requirement to keep ownership, assignment snapshots, and mention permissions aligned.
- Regenerate the workflow lock with the current upstream compiler while preserving executable dependency pins, telemetry correlation, and unlock hardening.

Relates to #56930; this fixes triage routing, not the coverage-output defect reported in that issue.
